title: Our Duty to the Next Generation Whether We Like It or Not, We Are Teaching Them
author: Chris Martin
source: The Ways of a Gentleman (Martin Substack), January 15, 2026
summary: Martin asserts that adults have an inescapable responsibility to teach the next generation through both intentional instruction and unintentional modeling. Every adult—whether parent, teacher, mentor, or simply an older person visible in the community—is educating young people about what matters, what is acceptable, what is worth pursuing. Martin emphasizes that the teaching happens whether we acknowledge it or not: through how we spend our time, how we treat others, how we handle failure, what we prioritize, and what standards we maintain or compromise. Parents and mentors cannot opt out of teaching; they can only choose whether to do it intentionally and thoughtfully or carelessly and haphazardly. Martin calls for a renewed sense of intergenerational responsibility and awareness of the profound influence older generations exert on the young.
points: Adults have an inescapable responsibility to teach the next generation through both intentional instruction and unintentional modeling—the teaching happens whether we acknowledge it or not.
Every adult is educating young people about what matters, what is acceptable, what is worth pursuing through how they spend time, treat others, handle failure, and maintain standards.
Parents and mentors cannot opt out of teaching—they can only choose whether to do it intentionally and thoughtfully or carelessly and haphazardly.
The most powerful teaching is often unconscious: young people absorb messages about integrity, courage, kindness, and character from observing the adults around them.
A renewed sense of intergenerational responsibility is essential—the adult generation must become aware of the profound influence it exerts on the young through daily choices and example.
